headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default: Airbyte can egress business data while LangGraph can read/write shared state and call external tools.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can expose business data through its API and broad egress, while LangGraph can read/write application files and ingest tool outputs into graph state. A shared workspace or copied outputs create a plausible injection bridge, though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty about the exact deployment pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into LangGraph prompts or files without sanitization
IF LangGraph nodes treat file or stdin content as instructions
IF both are deployed with a shared workspace or handoff channel
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiter wrapper around Airbyte outputs
Strip executable markup and tool directives before LangGraph ingestion
Use a separate staging file for raw Airbyte output
Require human review for any prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; LangGraph reads and writes filesystem state and sends data to model providers and developer-defined tools. In a shared workspace, Airbyte data can flow into LangGraph and then out to third parties by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive business data.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data from a shared source
IF LangGraph nodes forward that data to model providers or external tools
IF the two agents share files or graph state
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to non-sensitive sources
Place LangGraph in a separate workspace with no shared files
Disable external tool calls for nodes handling Airbyte output
Redact business data before passing it to LangGraph
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and egress broadly, while LangGraph can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read/write files, and use developer-defined tools. Their write surfaces overlap on shared application state even though LangGraph does not modify git and Airbyte has no filesystem write listed. The conflict is real in default orchestration but not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application directory or state store
IF LangGraph tools mutate files that Airbyte also reads
IF orchestration lacks locking or transactional coordination
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Add file locks around shared state writes
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Avoid concurrent runs on the same dataset
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce business-data outputs that LangGraph may treat as node inputs, and LangGraph can then act through tools or model-provider calls. Because LangGraph is a graph-of-agents framework with developer-wired tool execution, unverified Airbyte outputs can cascade into downstream actions by default unless explicitly checked.
conditions: IF LangGraph consumes Airbyte-produced records as authoritative inputs
IF downstream nodes trigger external actions based on those records
IF no verification or schema validation is inserted between them
mitigations: Validate Airbyte output against a schema before use
Insert a human approval step for action-taking nodes
Mark Airbyte data as untrusted in graph state
Log and diff transformed records before execution
requires-engineering: add verification nodes with typed contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte is documented as handling business data, while LangGraph handles graph state and model-provider API keys with broad network egress. If regulated or residency-bound business data is routed through LangGraph, retention and third-party processing policies can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed from Airbyte into LangGraph
IF LangGraph forwards prompts or state to external model providers
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the shared data
mitigations: Classify data before passing it into LangGraph
Keep regulated datasets out of LangGraph runs
Set short retention on graph state
Review provider DPAs and residency settings
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
